evidence.claim: Twenty shuffled round-robin schedules over the same transitive judgements recorded winner=alpha every time; unique_winners=['alpha']; unique_ranking_count=1.
Rock-paper-scissors judgements produce cycle_reported=true, winner=null, Copeland scores all 1. The cycle is reported rather than silently broken into a unique winner.

falsifiable_answer.discriminant: 20/20 round-robin shuffles elect alpha; cycle field winner=null and cycle_reported=true
falsifiable_answer.question: Is the resulting ranking order-independent — does shuffling the pairing schedule change the winner?

negative_controls.description: A rock-paper-scissors cycle must be reported; the module must not mint a silent Copeland/lex winner. Transitive control stays quiet.

residual_unknowns.claim: IMP-0264 tools/council/kernel.py is absent. This topology schedules and aggregates locally; it does not plug matches into a kernel event loop.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Replay a tournament through kernel.py once IMP-0264 lands and assert turn events equal played matches.

residual_unknowns.claim: IMP-0303 tools/council/vote/ballots.py is absent. Judgements here are an explicit pairwise table, not ballot-derived pairwise/Condorcet tallies.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Feed ballots.py pairwise outcomes into run_tournament and re-run the 20-shuffle and cycle probes.

residual_unknowns.claim: Swiss with 2 rounds on a 5-player field produced unique_winners=['NONE']. Incomplete Swiss is not claimed order-independent.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Run Swiss with n-1 rounds (round-robin equivalent) and compare the winner to complete round-robin.

reviewer.notes: Adversarial probe starts from the required tests. Cycle reports and withholds a winner; transitive field elects alpha and reports no cycle.
